_comment: KIT REGISTRY — the machine-readable half of the `kit` field in player-headshot-bank.md.
WHY THIS EXISTS (founder ruling 2026-08-04). The headshot bank was built for the World Cup
lane, so most banked faces wear a NATIONAL kit. The moment one of those heads sits under a
CLUB label the card contradicts itself: Erling Haaland in Norway red under a Manchester City
medallion, Raul Jimenez in Mexico green under Fulham, Vitinha in a Portugal collar under Paris
Saint-Germain. No crest and no photograph is involved, so nothing trips the D90 art gate. It is
a credibility problem instead: a Manchester City card showing red invites the reader to doubt
the numbers printed next to it, which is the exact opposite of what the sourcing discipline is
bought with.
THE CHECK IS COLOUR COMPATIBILITY, NOT OWNERSHIP. A head is not tied to one club. It carries a
kit COLOUR, and each label carries the body colours its club actually plays in. The guard asks
whether the head's colour is among the label's colours. That is what makes the two known-good
pairings pass on their merits rather than by exception: Bruno Fernandes is banked in a Portugal
red that is also Manchester United red, and Jude Bellingham in an England white that is also
Real Madrid white. Both survive because red really is United's colour, not because they were
special-cased.
BODY COLOURS ONLY. `colours` lists what the SHIRT IS, never its trim. Paris Saint-Germain is
listed blue and navy blue and NOT red, even though a red stripe runs down the chest. Admitting
trim would let a Portugal-red head pass under a Paris Saint-Germain label, which is one of the
three defects this file was written to stop.
SKY BLUE IS NOT BLUE. The colour tokens are matched exactly, with only the aliases below
treated as the same thing. Collapsing 'sky blue' into 'blue' would let a Chelsea head pass
under Manchester City, and the Haaland case is precisely a light-versus-dark failure.
AN UNREGISTERED HEAD IS A HARD FAILURE, NOT A PASS. A head with no row here has no known kit,
so the guard cannot clear it and refuses instead. Silence is how the drift returned the first
time. Adding a row is cheap: open the file as an image, read the shirt, write it down.
Every `kit` below was MEASURED off the artwork on the date shown, not copied from a prompt.
A prompt records what was asked for; only the pixels record what arrived.

MANCHESTER CITY.note: Sky blue home shirt. The 2026-27 shirt is a sky-blue-to-white gradient; the body colour is unchanged.
MANCHESTER CITY.source: Footy Headlines, Manchester City 26-27 home kit; ESPN Premier League 2026-27 kit round-up (retrieved 2026-08-04)

FULHAM.note: White shirt, black shorts. Red and black are trim only.

CRYSTAL PALACE.note: Red and blue vertical stripes are the club identity. The 2026-27 home shirt is a one-off anniversary design placing a red-and-blue sash on white; the identity colours are unchanged.
CRYSTAL PALACE.source: GiveMeSport, every Premier League home kit 26-27 (retrieved 2026-08-04)

PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN.note: Blue body. The red central stripe and its white edging are TRIM and are deliberately absent from this list.

AC MILAN.note: Red and black striped home shirt. White is listed on its merits, not as trim: the all-white change strip is the shirt AC Milan have worn in their most famous European finals and remains the standard away kit.

RC LENS.note: Sang et Or: blood-red and gold home shirt.

BRENTFORD.note: Red and white striped home shirt, black shorts. Striped since the 1925-26 season. Black is shorts and trim, never the body colour.

TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR.note: White home shirt, navy blue shorts. Navy is the SHORTS colour and is deliberately not listed: admitting it would let a navy head pass under this label.

CHELSEA.note: Royal blue home shirt. Not sky blue: the tokens are matched exactly and collapsing the two would let a Manchester City head pass here.

bruno-fernandes.note: A NATIONAL kit that legitimately clears a Manchester United label, because Portugal red and Manchester United red are the same colour. Kept as-is rather than regenerated: it passes the check on its merits.

anderson.note: Already a club head. England play in white; this one is red and clears Nottingham Forest.

baleba.note: Already a club head. Cameroon play in green; this one is blue and clears Brighton and Hove Albion.

haaland.note: THE NATIONAL HEAD. Correct under a Norway label and wrong under Manchester City. Superseded for club use by haaland-manchester-city. Retained, never overwritten.

jimenez.note: THE NATIONAL HEAD. Correct under a Mexico label and wrong under Fulham. Superseded for club use by jimenez-fulham. Retained, never overwritten.

wharton.note: Attributable to nothing. Charcoal is neither England white nor Crystal Palace red and blue, so this head clears no label at all and the guard refuses it everywhere. Superseded by wharton-crystal-palace. Retained, never overwritten.

vitinha.note: THE NATIONAL HEAD, red with a green collar trim. Correct under a Portugal label and wrong under Paris Saint-Germain. Superseded for club use by vitinha-paris-saint-germain. Retained, never overwritten.

pulisic.note: A NATIONAL kit that legitimately clears an AC Milan label: the warm cream-white body reads as Milan's traditional all-white change shirt. Kept as banked rather than regenerated; passes the check on its merits.

pulisic-tile.note: A NATIONAL kit that legitimately clears an AC Milan label: the warm cream-white body reads as Milan's traditional all-white change shirt. Kept as banked rather than regenerated; passes the check on its merits.

dembele.note: France blue clears Paris Saint-Germain blue, the same merit-pass as the banked Bruno Fernandes Portugal red under Manchester United.
